chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: Throwing the goat George and Bill Beason's career
summary: Jones taught Bill Beason his trick of flipping a goat; Beason left Louisville early for Horace Henderson's and Benny Carter's bands and later stopped playing.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And we had a big laugh, and were talking, and I was so glad to see him. And I couldn't get out of him what he was doing or where he'd been. He wasn't around the guys anymore. And we had so much fun talking different things. I had an old goat down there. We used to call him George.

Yeah, in Kentucky, in Louisville. So I could throw him, you know. I'd grab him by his horns, you know. I'd come up to him and pat him, 'Nice George. Nice George.' And all at once I'd grab him by his horns, and you'd twist his neck and he'd fall. Now when he falls over, you'd better be getting ready to run, you know, because when he gets up he's coming at you with them horns, you know.

So Bill Beeson come by one day, after practice, you know, after band practice. So he come by and I was showing him how to do it, you know, because he wanted to do it. So I said, "Be nice to him now, because he'll get mean after you throw him down. And be ready to run," I said. So Bill got him by the horns, turned him over, and he didn't go down enough, and I said, "Turn him some more. Don't turn him loose now." So Bill finally got him down but he didn't run. You know, this goat was behind him, he was tearing after Bill. Well, he wasn't too reckless, you know. He was all right. Then we had a lot of fun reminiscing about that. But I didn't get into why he doesn't play anymore or what, you know, because some guys don't like you to be getting into their business, you know. So I didn't know what had happened. I knew I could have used him many a time, you know.
Is that right? You could have used him.

Yeah, I would have been glad to use Bill, you know. He used to come back and tell me a lot. He left way before I did, and he'd come back to Kentucky, and we'd walk a lot and he would tell me what it was like, you know, being in big bands, with Benny Carter. First it was Horace Henderson's band.
Well, was he older than you?
No, he just got out a little bit quicker, you know. He got out a little quicker, you see. And as I say,
